title: Playing with Bill Cosby at the Lighthouse
summary: In Los Angeles Monk sat in with Cosby, who pays well and is a sharp devil's advocate.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: The strange thing is, that weekend I was supposed to submit this back to him, I think I had it ready for him the first of the week. That week, I had to go to Los Angeles, and I was in Los Angeles and I had called Bill Cosby. I gave him a buzz. He said, 'Well, what are you doing in town?' and so-and-so.

I said, 'I just came down for the weekend just to be with my boys.' He said, 'Well, I'm doing a thing at the Lighthouse Sunday night. Why don't you come out and play with me?' And I said, 'Well, I didn't come down here to play. I haven't got my bass or anything.' He said, 'Well, you can get a bass, and come on out. Just come on out and play.' He said, 'Don't worry about it. I'll take care of you, ere you hang up.' Well, we always do that.

So I want to go too. And it was great, to go out to the Lighthouse and a chance to hang out and be with that clown, too, which was a lot of fun. I got a bass and went out. Because it was a gig for me, he always paid. He paid so good you couldn't... He made you an offer you couldn't refuse, when you played with him.

So I went out and made this gig and it was a great... And I was saying, 'You know, Bill, I got something I want you to see.' Because all along, even until today, when something happens for me that I think makes me bubble inside, I find myself talking it over with Bill. He is one of the greatest devil's advocates you can find. And it don't take him a long time to sit and think it out. And I always respect his opinions.
He would go through the challenges with you and...

He would go through it with you and, like, you always feel, if this guy don't find it, can't find the holes in it, there's no holes in it. Because he leans that way with his ideas and thoughts anyhow. And he's a bright man, a very bright man. A funny man, but he's a very bright man.
